title.source: Section check: Who builds AI, and at what cost
title.back: Section check: Who builds AI, and what it costs

intro.source: 8 questions about Lessons 5–8. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 8 questions about Lessons 5–8. No need to hurry. You can go back to the lessons and try again as many times as you like.

questions.0.question.source: Like clothes, an AI tool has a supply chain. What is a supply chain?
questions.0.question.back: Like clothes, an AI tool has a supply chain. What is a supply chain?

questions.0.options.0.text.source: The people who help make it, step by step
questions.0.options.0.text.back: The people who help make it, step by step

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A supply chain is all the people and places that help to make a product. Some of them stay hidden.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. A supply chain is all the people and places that help make a product. Some of them are hidden.

questions.0.options.1.text.source: A list of rules that say how the tool must work
questions.0.options.1.text.back: A list of rules for how the tool must work

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Rules are not a supply chain. A supply chain is the people who help make a product. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Rules are not a supply chain. A supply chain is the people who help make a product. Go back to Lesson 5.

questions.0.options.2.text.source: A shop where people can buy the tool
questions.0.options.2.text.back: A shop where people can buy this tool

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A shop sells a product. A supply chain is all the people who help to make it. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A shop sells a product, while a supply chain is all the people who help make that product. Go back to Lesson 5.

questions.1.question.source: In 2023, Oxford researchers checked 15 online work platforms. What did they find?
questions.1.question.back: In 2023, researchers from Oxford checked 15 online work platforms. What did they find?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: Every platform paid all workers fairly
questions.1.options.0.text.back: Every platform paid all workers fairly

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The researchers found low pay and a lot of unpaid time. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The researchers found low pay and a lot of unpaid time. Go back to Lesson 5.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: Workers were paid for every hour they spent
questions.1.options.1.text.back: Workers were paid for every hour they worked

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. More than a quarter of the workers' time was unpaid, such as time looking for tasks. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. More than a quarter of the workers' time was unpaid, such as time spent looking for tasks. Go back to Lesson 5.

questions.1.options.2.text.source: None met all of their basic standards
questions.1.options.2.text.back: None passed all of their basic standards

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. The best platform scored only 5 out of 10. Some platforms changed their rules after the study.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. The best platform scored only 5 out of 10. After this study, some platforms changed their rules.

questions.2.question.source: Why do many data centres use water?
questions.2.question.back: Why do many data centres use water?

questions.2.options.0.text.source: To make the power that the chips use
questions.2.options.0.text.back: To make the electricity the chips use

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Data centres use a lot of electricity, but the water does not make it. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Data centres use a lot of electricity, but the water is not used to make it. Go back to Lesson 6.

questions.2.options.1.text.source: To cool chips that get very hot
questions.2.options.1.text.back: To cool chips that get very hot

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The chips use a lot of electricity and get very hot. Water helps to cool them.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. The chips use a lot of electricity and get very hot. Water helps cool them down.

questions.2.options.2.text.source: To wash the dust off the computers
questions.2.options.2.text.back: To wash the dust off the computers

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The water is not for cleaning. It helps with the heat. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The water is not for cleaning; it helps with the heat. Go back to Lesson 6.

questions.3.stimulus.title.back: A made-up plan to build a data centre

questions.3.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. A company plans a data centre in the made-up town of Westvale. It says about 800 people will help to build it over two years. About 40 people will work there after it opens.
questions.3.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. A company plans to build a data centre in Westvale, a made-up town. The company says about 800 people will help build it over two years. After it opens, about 40 people will work there.

questions.3.question.source: A man in the town says, “This will give 800 people work for years.” What is wrong with this?
questions.3.question.back: A man in the town says, "This centre will give 800 people work for many years." What is wrong with what he said?

questions.3.options.0.text.source: The building work lasts only two years
questions.3.options.0.text.back: The building work lasts only two years

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Building work ends when the building is finished. After that, there are only about 40 jobs.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. Building work ends when the building is finished. After that there are only about 40 jobs.

questions.3.options.1.text.source: Data centres need nobody to build them
questions.3.options.1.text.back: Data centres need no people to build them

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The company says about 800 people will help to build it. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The company says about 800 people will help build it. Go back to Lesson 6.

questions.3.options.2.text.source: All 800 people will work inside it later
questions.3.options.2.text.back: All 800 people will work inside it later

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Only about 40 people will work there after it opens. Look back at Lesson 6.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. After it opens, only about 40 people will work there. Go back to Lesson 6.

questions.4.question.source: In Harbourside, few people publish books in Language C. What does “publish” mean?
questions.4.question.back: In Harbourside, very few people publish books in Language C. What does "publish" mean?

questions.4.options.0.text.source: To speak a language at home
questions.4.options.0.text.back: To speak a language at home

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. People speak Language C a lot. To publish means to put out writing. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. People speak Language C a lot. Publishing means putting out writing. Go back to Lesson 7.

questions.4.options.1.text.source: To change words into another language
questions.4.options.1.text.back: To change words into another language

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. That is to translate. To publish is to put out writing for many people. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. That is translating. Publishing is putting out writing for many people. Go back to Lesson 7.

questions.4.options.2.text.source: To put out writing for many to read
questions.4.options.2.text.back: To put out writing for many people to read

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. To publish is to print or put out writing. Little is published in Language C, so AI has little to learn from.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. Publishing is printing or putting out writing. Little is published in Language C, so AI has little to learn from.

questions.5.question.source: Why do some languages have much more writing than others?
questions.5.question.back: Why do some languages have much more writing than others?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: Some languages are much harder to write
questions.5.options.0.text.back: Some languages are much harder to write

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. It is not about how hard a language is. It depends on how a language has been used. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. This is not about how hard a language is. It depends on how the language has been used. Go back to Lesson 7.

questions.5.options.1.text.source: History, such as which ones schools use
questions.5.options.1.text.back: History, such as which language schools use

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. It depends on history: which languages schools, books, news and governments use, and what people type online.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. It depends on history: which languages schools, books, news and governments use, and what people type on the internet.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: The more speakers, the more writing
questions.5.options.2.text.back: The more speakers, the more writing

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. In Harbourside, Language C has the most speakers but very little writing. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. In Harbourside, Language C has the most speakers but very little writing. Go back to Lesson 7.

questions.6.question.source: About 45% of a famous photo collection came from the United States, and about 2% from India. What does this help to explain?
questions.6.question.back: About 45 percent of the photos in one famous photo collection came from the United States, and about 2 percent from India. What does this information help explain?

questions.6.options.0.text.source: Why a tool did worse with photos from India
questions.6.options.0.text.back: Why a tool did worse with photos from India

questions.6.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Few photos came from India, so the data did not represent it well. A tool trained on it did worse there.
questions.6.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. There were few photos from India, so the data did not represent India well. A tool trained on this data did worse there.

questions.6.options.1.text.source: Why the tool did better with photos from India
questions.6.options.1.text.back: Why the tool did better with photos from India

questions.6.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. With so few photos from India, the tool did worse there, not better. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.6.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. There were very few photos from India, so the tool did worse there, not better. Go back to Lesson 8.

questions.6.options.2.text.source: Why people in India took fewer photos
questions.6.options.2.text.back: Why people in India took fewer photos

questions.6.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The numbers show what is in the collection. They do not show how many photos people took. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.6.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The numbers show what is in the collection. They do not show how many photos people took. Go back to Lesson 8.

questions.7.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. At the made-up Stonebay market, a tool names fish from photos. It names river fish well, but it often gets sea fish wrong. Almost all of its training photos show river fish.
questions.7.stimulus.body.note: "River fish" is ปลาน้ำจืด (freshwater fish), the everyday Thai term; a literal ปลาแม่น้ำ sounds odd. Check it still reads as the river/sea contrast.
questions.7.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. At Stonebay market, a made-up market, there is a tool that names fish from photos. It names freshwater fish well, but often names sea fish wrongly. Almost all of its training photos are of freshwater fish.

questions.7.question.source: What would most likely help the tool?
questions.7.question.back: What would most likely help this tool?

questions.7.options.0.text.source: Add more photos of river fish
questions.7.options.0.text.back: Add more photos of freshwater fish

questions.7.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. It already knows river fish well. More of the same kind will not fill the gap. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.7.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. It already knows freshwater fish well. Adding more of the same kind does not fill that gap. Go back to Lesson 8.

questions.7.options.1.text.source: Add labelled photos of sea fish
questions.7.options.1.text.back: Add photos of sea fish with labels

questions.7.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Its training data does not represent sea fish. Labelled photos of sea fish can fill that gap.
questions.7.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. Its training data does not represent sea fish. Labelled photos of sea fish can fill that gap.

questions.7.options.2.text.source: Use the tool only when it is sunny
questions.7.options.2.text.back: Use the tool only when it is sunny

questions.7.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The light is not the problem. The problem is what its training photos show. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.7.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The light is not the problem. The problem is what its training photos show. Go back to Lesson 8.

results.high.source: Well done. You can see the people, the planet and the languages behind AI tools.
results.high.back: Well done. You can see the people, our planet and the languages behind AI tools.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Good work. You answered many right. Go back to the lessons for the ones you have not got right yet, then try again if you want to.

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 5–8, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Go back to Lessons 5–8, then try again. Take as long as you need.
